text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: CUDA OOM on node gpu-prod-17 despite headroom reported. Alerts triggered for 3 pods in pool 'inference-high'. Incident channel opened.

maria: I'm on it. first glance — looks like a ~1s microburst of allocations from prefetch + kv-cache fill.

raj: can you paste the node-level `nvidia-smi` and allocator traces?

maria: paste below. `kubectl logs -n infra gpu-serv-74 -c runtime --since=2m` shows repeated `cudaMalloc` failures.

```
# nvidia-smi top
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
| 17   A100-SXM4-80GB    Off   | 00000000:3X:00.0 Off | 0                    |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Processes:                                                       GPU Memory |
|  PID   Type   Process name                             Usage      |
|  4321  C      python3                                       76MiB   |
|  8764  C      runtime_server                               45GiB   |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

logs snippet: ```
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] allocation attempt: 524288000 bytes
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] cudaMalloc -> OUT_OF_MEMORY
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] headroom_available=12.2GiB, reserved_pool_free=11.9GiB
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] kv_cache_reserve: pinned=3GiB, spilled=0
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] spare_pool_gap=512MiB
```

maria: so allocator thinks there's ~11.9GiB free in reserved_pool but cudaMalloc fails on a 500MB chunk.

raj: smells like fragmentation + large contiguous allocation requirement. any calls to prefetch that request contiguous pinned buffers?

maria: yes — model prefetcher requests large contiguous tensors for attention map preallocation. It runs concurrent prefetch for 8 requests in that burst.

kori: @maria tag: customer-impact? are any customer requests timed out?

maria: customer-success, we saw ~50 requests fail across two downstream endpoints between 09:12:02-09:12:14. Most recovered after container restart. Latency spike to ~12s. Looks partial impact (small % of requests for heavy seq models).

derek: oncall-sre, recommend mitigation: 1) throttle prefetch concurrency 2) temporarily increase spare_pool slack config 3) cordon + drain node if fragmentation persists.

sre-ops-bot: suggested runbook "oom-fragmentation-quick-mitigations" invoked by maria at 09:18.

maria: applying mitigation 1 now — set `PREFETCH_CONCURRENCY=2` on pool 'inference-high' via runtime-config.

```
# apply change
kubectl set env deployment/runtime-prod -n infra PREFETCH_CONCURRENCY=2
```

maria: rolling patch deployed. monitoring.

(2m)

raj: telemetry shows microburst rate drop. errors reduced but one more OOM at 09:20 on same node. checking allocator slab map...

maria: slab map excerpt (simplified): `free_chunks: [64MiB x 3, 128MiB x 2, 256MiB x 1, fragmented_free=~11.7GiB but largest_contiguous=192MiB]`

raj: there's the kicker — heuristics report total free but largest contiguous is small. large allocations fail even with >10GiB total free.

derek: this aligns with our fragmentation hypothesis from the allocator design: reserved blocks broken into many scattered small runs by prior evictions and pinned kv-cache blocks.

maria: immediate extra mitigation: set `PREFETCH_CONTIGUOUS=false` for that variant so it uses chunked allocations instead of one giant allocation. pushing config.

maria: also nudging spare pool: `SPARE_POOL_TARGET=14GB` up from 12GB on node group via autoscaler override (temporary). applying.

sre-ops-bot: note — increasing spare pool will reduce capacity and may affect throughput.

oncall-bot: handoff in 2h to raj for escalation window. Please document steps taken.

(10m)

maria: after both changes: no further OOMs in 12m window on that node. traffic normalized.

customer-success: sending heads-up to affected customers: short blip, some timeouts on long-seq models, mitigated, monitoring. Draft message preview attached.

customer-success: "We're aware of an intermittent capacity error affecting a subset of requests for long-sequence models between 09:12-09:20 UTC. A mitigation has been applied and we don't expect ongoing impact. We'll follow up with a post-incident summary."

kori: thanks. next steps for postmortem?

raj: proposed action items: 1) root cause analysis on allocator fragmentation triggers (eviction policy + pinned kv-cache churn) 2) implement a best-effort fast-path that falls back to chunked allocation when largest_contiguous < requested_size and avoid immediate OOM 3) add synthetic microburst test for prefetch concurrency in e2e tests 4) permanent tuning for spare_pool sizing and prefetch defaults by model family.

maria: I'll capture telemetry slices and create a bug with allocator slab dumps attached.

derek: also add an autoscaler policy: if fragmentation detected and free_total >> required but largest_contiguous small, proactively schedule a node rotation or enable local compaction if possible.

oncall-bot: raj is primary for follow-ups, scheduled handoff note: 11:12 UTC.

maria: logging final: `incident resolved - mitigations applied (prefetch throttled, contiguous off, spare_pool increased)`. will open postmortem doc.

incident-bot: incident closed (temporary mitigation in place). please assign postmortem and label severity P2.

raj: assigning to `eng-runtime` and `eng-ml`. I'll own the RCA and compaction proposal.

kori: noted, CS will prepare customer comms for tomorrow with root cause summary.

-- end of thread --
